there are possible benefits towards education, they find that very young children 
co-watching educational content with an adult regularly socially engaging with 
them, can enhance their language and cognitive development. Despite this there 
seems to be little research regarding the positive educational effects of screen 
time on teenagers. 
With the rise of social media platforms in the 2010s and the more recent short-
form content platforms such as TikTok, raises questions on their phycological 
effects. An empirical review by (Wilmer, et al., 2017) finds that people with 
higher levels of social media usage are more likely to prefer immediate 
gratification over delayed rewards, and with extensive usage is associated with a 
reduced attention spans. (Wilmer, et al., 2017) also found these people have a 
reduced working memory; by this cognitive load theory would suggest, that a 
reduced short-term working memory would intern reduce the quantity of 
information that can be stored into long term memory. 
In a study by (Jeongmin, et al., 2014), showed that increased addiction to smart 
phones led to a lower quality of self-regulated learning, caused by a lack of self-
control when ignoring distracting notifications. (Chen, et al., 2022) discuss the 
differences between addicted and non-addicted users of short-form content 
platforms. They found that in both groups they had good attention during 
shorter videos, and during longer videos the addicted users became distracted.
